question: How much revenue do missed calls cost Punctual Pros?
html:
What Missed Calls Cost Punctual Pros

Missed inbound calls cost Punctual Pros an estimated ~$1.37M a year in recoverable jobs, about 6% of est. revenue. That figure comes from a conservative model and has not been checked against company call data (Voice AI research).

How the estimate works

  • Inbound calls are est. at ~3,502 a month. Volume is backed out of the ~$22M revenue estimate, not measured (Voice AI research; Punctual Pros public filings).
  • An est. 14.8% of calls are missed. This blends 12% after-hours share × 35% lost with 88% daytime share × 12% missed. That is roughly 6,200 missed calls a year (est.).
  • Recovered revenue is about 1,343 jobs × $1,024 average ticket. That splits into ~$390K after-hours and ~$982K daytime or storm overflow (est.).
InputValue (est.)
Missed share14.8% (range 10–35%)
Share recovered by AI80%
Booking rate45%
Incrementality60% (40% would have called back)
Average ticket$1,024

Why it may run higher

  • Industry benchmarks are worse than the base case. Only 52% of home-services callers reach a person, or 65% of calls over 15 seconds (Voice AI research).
  • Off-hours calls peak in summer, at 14.1% of HVAC inbound in June versus 9.8% in October (Punctual Pros demand model).
  • The model stops at recoverable jobs. It does not count membership or tune-up follow-on value.
  • A separate outbound renewal lift adds ~$403K. That assumes 6,000 members, which is not public. Combined, the total is ~$1.78M, about 8.1% of est. revenue (Voice AI research).

Why confidence is limited

  • The revenue base is itself an estimate: ~$22M, range $16–28M, medium confidence (Punctual Pros public filings). Call volume moves with it.
  • Booking and recovery rates come from vendors. They are self-reported and unaudited (Voice AI research).
  • Actual call volume, missed-call rate, booking rate, ticket size and member count are not in the context.

Data that would settle it

  • ServiceTitan or phone-system logs covering answered, abandoned and after-hours calls by trade and month.
  • Booked-job conversion by CSR and by hour.
  • Average ticket by trade, plus a callback match rate to test the 60% incrementality assumption.

Next actions

  1. Pull 12 months of Punctual Pros call and booking data. Rerun the model with actual missed share, booking rate and ticket.
  2. Load the same history into the demand model. Fit weather and seasonal elasticities, and size peak-week overflow.
  3. Pilot an AI after-hours answering service in one PA territory. Measure incremental booked jobs against a control territory.
  4. Confirm the membership count and renewal rate before counting the outbound upside in the growth plan.
markdown:
# What Missed Calls Cost Punctual Pros

Missed inbound calls cost Punctual Pros an estimated **~$1.37M a year** in recoverable jobs, about 6% of est. revenue. That figure comes from a conservative model and has not been checked against company call data (Voice AI research).

## How the estimate works

- Inbound calls are est. at ~3,502 a month. Volume is backed out of the ~$22M revenue estimate, not measured (Voice AI research; Punctual Pros public filings).
- An est. 14.8% of calls are missed. This blends 12% after-hours share × 35% lost with 88% daytime share × 12% missed. That is roughly 6,200 missed calls a year (est.).
- Recovered revenue is about 1,343 jobs × $1,024 average ticket. That splits into ~$390K after-hours and ~$982K daytime or storm overflow (est.).

| Input | Value (est.) |
|---|---|
| Missed share | 14.8% (range 10–35%) |
| Share recovered by AI | 80% |
| Booking rate | 45% |
| Incrementality | 60% (40% would have called back) |
| Average ticket | $1,024 |

## Why it may run higher

- Industry benchmarks are worse than the base case. Only 52% of home-services callers reach a person, or 65% of calls over 15 seconds (Voice AI research).
- Off-hours calls peak in summer, at 14.1% of HVAC inbound in June versus 9.8% in October (Punctual Pros demand model).
- The model stops at recoverable jobs. It does not count membership or tune-up follow-on value.
- A separate outbound renewal lift adds ~$403K. That assumes 6,000 members, which is not public. Combined, the total is ~$1.78M, about 8.1% of est. revenue (Voice AI research).

## Why confidence is limited

- The revenue base is itself an estimate: ~$22M, range $16–28M, medium confidence (Punctual Pros public filings). Call volume moves with it.
- Booking and recovery rates come from vendors. They are self-reported and unaudited (Voice AI research).
- Actual call volume, missed-call rate, booking rate, ticket size and member count are not in the context.

## Data that would settle it

- ServiceTitan or phone-system logs covering answered, abandoned and after-hours calls by trade and month.
- Booked-job conversion by CSR and by hour.
- Average ticket by trade, plus a callback match rate to test the 60% incrementality assumption.

## Next actions

1. Pull 12 months of Punctual Pros call and booking data. Rerun the model with actual missed share, booking rate and ticket.
2. Load the same history into the demand model. Fit weather and seasonal elasticities, and size peak-week overflow.
3. Pilot an AI after-hours answering service in one PA territory. Measure incremental booked jobs against a control territory.
4. Confirm the membership count and renewal rate before counting the outbound upside in the growth plan.
